Surah Saba' (Makkan except for verse 2 which is Madani; its verses are 54 or 55; it was revealed after Luqman)

﴿All praise is due to Allah﴾ He praised Himself with this, and what is meant by it is the extolling of Him with its content, from the establishment of praise, which is the attribution of beauty to Allah the Exalted. ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ in ownership and in creation. ﴿And to Him is the praise in the Hereafter﴾, just as in this world; His friends will praise Him when they enter Paradise. ﴿And He is the All-Wise﴾ in His actions, ﴿the All-Aware﴾ of His creation.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 34, verse 2:

﴿He knows what enters into the earth﴾ (yadkhul) into it, like water and other things, ﴿and what comes out of it﴾ and ﴿what descends from the sky﴾ of provision and other things, ﴿and what ascends into it﴾ (yasʿad) into it, of deeds and other things, ﴿and He is the Most Merciful﴾ toward His friends (awliya'ihi), ﴿the Oft-Forgiving﴾ toward them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 34, verse 3:

﴿And those who disbelieve say: "The Hour will not come to us."﴾ (al-Sā'a) the Resurrection (al-Qiyāma). ﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿"Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come to you, the Knower of the unseen,"﴾ (ʿĀlim al-Ghayb) — in the genitive (bi-l-jarr) as an adjective (ṣifa), and in the nominative (bi-l-raf') as the predicate (khabar) of an omitted subject (mubtada'); and ʿAllām in the genitive (bi-l-jarr) — ﴿"from Whom there is not hidden"﴾ (ya'zub) it is concealed (yaghīb) ﴿"from Him the weight"﴾ (mithqāl) (i.e., the measure) ﴿"of an atom"﴾ (dharra), the smallest ant (aṣghar namla) ﴿"in the heavens or on the earth, nor anything smaller than that, nor greater, but it is in a clear Book"﴾ (mubīn), manifest (bayyin); it is the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawḥ al-Maḥfūẓ), and it is good (ḥasan) in Paradise.
﴿That He may reward﴾ therein ﴿those who believe and do righteous deeds. For them is forgiveness and generous provision﴾, good, in Paradise.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 34, verse 5:

﴿And those who strive against﴾ the invalidation of ﴿Our signs﴾, the Qur'an, ﴿seeking to frustrate [them]﴾. In another reading, here and in what comes later, it is read as mu'ajizin (مُعاجِزِينَ), meaning: deeming Our powerlessness [to be possible], or competing with Us so that they escape Us, because they assume there is no resurrection and no punishment. ﴿For those there is a punishment of a painful kind of torment﴾, an evil torment, ﴿painful﴾, causing pain. It is read with a genitive and with a nominative ending as an attributive adjective of rijzin (رِجْزٍ), or of ʿadhab (عَذاب).

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 34, verse 6:

﴿And those who have been given knowledge﴾ know, ﴿see﴾ [i.e., know] ﴿that what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾ — that is, the Qur'an — ﴿is the truth﴾, the word "huwa" (it) being a separating pronoun (damir fasl), ﴿and it guides to the path﴾ — the way — ﴿of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy﴾, that is, Allah, the Possessor of might, the One worthy of praise.

Note on the text: the passage names those "given knowledge" as the believers among the People of the Book, such as ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam and his companions.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 34, verse 7:

﴿And those who disbelieved said﴾ i.e., some of them said to others, in a tone of astonishment, ﴿"Shall we direct you to a man﴾ who is Muhammad, ﴿who will inform you﴾ that is, tell you, ﴿that when you have been torn apart﴾ that is, cut into pieces ﴿completely [kull mumazzaq]﴾ with the meaning of tearing apart?"﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 34, verse 8:

﴿Has he invented a lie against Allah, or is there madness in him?﴾ (the hamzah is opened for interrogation, and it is used without the hamzat al-wasl) ﴿against Allah, a lie﴾ in the Qur'an, ﴿or is there madness in him?﴾ (jinnah: insanity), he imagined that ﴿Rather, those who do not believe in the Hereafter﴾ (which comprises the resurrection and the punishment) ﴿are in the punishment﴾ (in the punishment in the Hereafter) ﴿and in far error﴾ (far from the truth in this world).

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti) on Surah 34, verse 9:

﴿Have they not looked﴾ (yanẓurū) ﴿at what is before them and what is behind them﴾, meaning what is above them and what is below them, ﴿of the heaven and the earth? If We willed, We could cause the earth to swallow them, or cause a piece (kisfan) of the sky to fall upon them.﴾ It is read with the sin sukūn (kisf) and with fatḥa (kisaf), meaning "pieces" (qiṭaʿan). In another reading, the three verbs (nakhsif, nusqit, and the implied verb) are read with the letter yāʾ (yakhsif, yusqit). ﴿Indeed, in that﴾ which is seen ﴿is a sign for every servant who turns back﴾ (munīb) to his Lord, which points to God's power over resurrection and whatever He wills.

And We had certainly bestowed upon David a bounty from Us: prophethood and a scripture. And We said, ﴿O mountains, echo back﴾, meaning, return [the praise] ﴿with him﴾ in glorification, ﴿and the birds﴾, [the word] "al-tayr" being in the accusative case, coordinated with the grammatical position (*mahall*) of "al-jibal" (the mountains). That is, We called them to glorify along with him. ﴿And We made iron soft for him﴾, so that it became in his hand like dough.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 34, verse 11:

And We said, ﴿Make full coats of mail﴾ from it, ﴿wide-flowing﴾, meaning complete coats of mail that their wearer drags upon the earth, ﴿and measure well the links﴾, meaning the weaving of the coats of mail. It was said that the maker of them is called a sarrad (a maker of coats of mail), meaning: make it such that its rings are proportionate. ﴿And work righteousness﴾, meaning you, the family of Dawud along with him. ﴿Indeed, I am Seeing of what you do﴾, Seeing of what you do, so I will recompense you for it.

And to Solomon (We subjected) the wind; (its) morning (course) was a month's journey and its evening (course) a month's journey. (The reading with raf', "al-rih" in the nominative, is with the implied meaning "its subjugation" [taskhir]). Its morning course: its travel from the ghudwa (the morning, al-saba) until midday (al-zawal), a month's journey. Its evening course: its travel from midday until sunset (al-ghurub), a month's journey. We melted for him the spring of molten copper (qitr), i.e., brass (nuhas), so it flowed for three days with their nights, like the flowing of water, and people worked with it until today, of what was given to Solomon. ﴿And of the jinn, whoever worked before him by the permission﴾ by the command ﴿of his Lord. And whoever of them deviates﴾ turns aside ﴿from Our command﴾ to him, by obeying him, ﴿We will make him taste of the punishment of the Blaze﴾ the Fire, in the Hereafter. It was also said that (this punishment is) in this world, by an angel striking him with a whip of fire, a blow that burns him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 34, verse 13:

﴿They made for him whatever he willed: sanctuaries (maḥārīb), that is, lofty structures to which one ascends by stairs; and images (tamāthīl), the plural of timthāl, which is everything that you make resembling something else, that is, statues made of copper, glass and marble; and the making of images was not forbidden in his law; and basins (jifān), the plural of jafna, and like reservoirs (al-jawāb), the plural of jābiyah, which is a large basin around which a thousand men gather to eat from one bowl; and cooking pots (qudūr) fixed (rāsiyāt), firm, having legs, not moving from their places, made from the mountains in Yemen, to which one ascends by ladders.﴾ And We said: ﴿Work, O family of Dawud,﴾ in obedience to God, ﴿in gratitude﴾ to Him for what He has given you. ﴿And few of My servants are grateful.﴾ Those who act in obedience to Me in thanks for My blessing.

Then, when We decreed death upon him (upon Sulayman), he remained standing, leaning on his staff, dead for a year, while the jinn continued doing those arduous tasks as was their custom, unaware of his death, until the termite (al-arada) ate away his staff, and he fell down dead. ﴿Nothing showed them his death except a creature of the earth﴾: the verbal noun of "aradat al-khashaba" (the wood was eaten by termites), in the passive form, meaning "the termites ate it." ﴿eating away at his staff﴾: with hamza and without it (with an alif), meaning his staff, because by it one is driven away and rebuked (yunsa, i.e., driven off, chased away with it). ﴿So when he fell﴾ dead, ﴿the jinn saw clearly﴾, it became evident to them. ﴿That﴾ here is light (mukhaffafa), meaning that they ﴿had they known the unseen﴾, and among it what was hidden from them of Sulayman's death, ﴿they would not have remained in the humiliating torment﴾, the arduous labour imposed on them, because they had assumed he was alive, which was contrary to their assumption. The knowledge of the unseen and the knowledge of its occurrence follow a pattern, by calculating what the termites ate of the staff after his death, for example a day and a night.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 34, verse 15:

﴿Indeed there was for Saba' (with or without tanwin, a tribe named after an ancestor of theirs from the Arabs)﴾ ﴿in their dwelling place﴾ in Yemen ﴿a sign﴾ indicating the power of God the Exalted: ﴿two gardens﴾ (a substitution for ﴿on the right and on the left﴾), on the right and on the left of their valley ﴿Eat of the provision of your Lord and be grateful to Him﴾ for what He has provided you of blessings ﴿in a good land﴾ in the land of Saba', where there are no salt marshes, no mosquito, no fly, no bedbug, no scorpion and no snake, and a stranger passes through it with lice in his clothes and they die because of the goodness of its air. ﴿And [God is] a Lord, Forgiving﴾

﴿So they turned away﴾ from His gratitude and disbelieved. ﴿So We sent upon them the flood of al-Arim﴾. Al-Arim is the plural of ʿarima, which is that which holds back water, whether a masonry dam or something else, until the time it is needed. That is, the flood of their valley, which had been held back by what has been mentioned, so it drowned their two gardens and their property. ﴿And We replaced their two gardens with two gardens﴾ of ذَواتَيْ (dhawatay), the dual of dhawat, which is the singular on its original form, ﴿bearing أُكُل خَمْط (ukul khamt)﴾, meaning bitter and foul. The word أُكُل may be read with an idafa (construct), in the sense of ma'kul (that which is eaten), or without it, and khamt is conjoined to it.

﴿That﴾ the alteration, ﴿We recompensed them for what they disbelieved﴾ for their disbelief, ﴿And do We recompense any but the ungrateful?﴾ Read with the ya' and the nun (نُجَازِي), with a kasra on the zay, and the kafur in the accusative (الكَفُورَ). That is: none is called to account except him.

And We placed between them—between Saba' and those in Yemen—and between the towns which We had blessed with water and trees, which are the towns of Syria to which they travel for trade—visible towns, connected from Yemen to Syria. And We measured the travel among them, such that they would take a noon rest (qayl) in one town and spend the night in another, until the end of their journey, and they would not need to carry provisions or water. That is, We said: ﴿Travel among them by night and by day, safe and secure.﴾ You shall not fear in night or in day.

Then they said, "Our Lord, lengthen [bu'‘id] the distance between our journeys," and in another reading, "make [it] distant" (ba‘id), [meaning, to the Levant] make them deserts, so that they might look down on the poor by riding mounts and carrying provisions and water; thus they became ungrateful for the blessing. ﴿And they wronged themselves﴾ by disbelief. ﴿So We made them into tales﴾ for those who came after them concerning that. ﴿And We scattered them completely﴾, i.e., We dispersed them throughout the lands with complete dispersal. ﴿Indeed in that﴾ mentioned [matter] ﴿are signs﴾, lessons, ﴿for every steadfast one﴾ in refraining from sins, ﴿grateful﴾ for blessings.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn, a classical Qur'anic commentary) on Surah 34, verse 20:

﴿And indeed Iblis found his assumption about them to be true﴾, read as "ṣadaqa" with the light pronunciation (بِالتَّخْفِيفِ) and with the emphatic pronunciation (وَالتَّشْدِيد), ﴿upon them﴾, i.e., the disbelievers among them, of Saba' (﴿سَبَأ﴾), ﴿Iblis his assumption﴾, that by his seduction they would follow him, ﴿so they followed him﴾. So "ṣadaqa" with the light pronunciation (بِالتَّخْفِيفِ) means in his assumption, or "ṣadaqa" with the emphatic pronunciation (بِالتَّشْدِيدِ) means his assumption, i.e., he found it true. ﴿Except﴾, with the meaning of "lākin" (لَكِنْ, "but"), ﴿a group of the believers﴾, where "min" (مِن) is for specification (لِلْبَيانِ), i.e., they are the believers who did not follow him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 34, verse 21:

﴿And he had no authority over them﴾ [i.e., no domination or compulsion] ﴿except that We might make evident (ʿilm ẓuhūr, knowledge of manifestation) who believes in the Hereafter from those who are in doubt concerning it﴾, so that We may recompense each of the two groups, ﴿and your Lord is Guardian over all things﴾ [i.e., Watchful over them].

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 34, verse 22:

﴿Say﴾ O Muhammad, to the disbelievers of Makkah, ﴿Call upon those you claimed﴾, i.e., you claimed them to be gods, ﴿besides Allah﴾, i.e., other than Him, so that they may benefit you according to your claim. He, the Exalted, said concerning them: ﴿They do not possess an atom's weight﴾, i.e., the weight of ﴿a dhharrah﴾ (a tiny ant, or a mote of dust), ﴿of good or evil in the heavens or on the earth. And they have no share in them [i.e., in the heavens and the earth], and He has no helper among them﴾, i.e., among the gods, ﴿from among them﴾, meaning ﴿a supporter﴾, i.e., an assistant.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn, Qur'anic exegesis) on surah 34, verse 23:

﴿And intercession does not benefit with Him﴾. This refutes their claim that their gods intercede with Him, ﴿except for one whom He has permitted﴾, with the hamza of the verb أَذِنَ (ʾadhina, "permitted") read with a fatha and with a damma, ﴿to do so﴾ in intercession. ﴿Until, when terror is removed﴾, with the verb فُزِّعَ (fuzziʿa) read in both the active and the passive form, ﴿from their hearts﴾, meaning the terror is lifted from them by the granting of permission for it. ﴿They say﴾, meaning some of them say to others, rejoicing, ﴿"What has your Lord said?"﴾ regarding it. ﴿They say﴾, meaning the saying is ﴿"The truth"﴾, that is, He has granted permission for it. ﴿And He is the Most High﴾, exalted above His creation by dominance, ﴿the Great﴾, the Magnificent.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 34, verse 24:

﴿Say: "Who provides for you from the heavens?"﴾ (i.e., the rain) ﴿and the earth?﴾ (i.e., the plants) ﴿Say: "Allah."﴾ If they do not say it, there is no other answer. ﴿And indeed we or you are surely upon guidance or in clear error.﴾ That is, one of the two parties. ﴿The ambiguity is a gentle way of inviting them to faith, if they are granted success in it.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 34, verse 25:

﴿Say: "You will not be asked about what we committed of sin"﴾ (ajramna) meaning: we sinned, ﴿and we will not be asked about what you do﴾ because we are free of you (bari'un).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 34, verse 26:

﴿Say: "Our Lord will bring us together"﴾ on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿then He will judge﴾ (yahkum, i.e., decide) ﴿between us with truth﴾, so He will admit the people of truth into Paradise and the people of falsehood into the Fire. ﴿And He is the Judge (al-Fattah), the All-Knowing﴾, the Judge (al-Hakim) ﴿who knows﴾ what He judges by.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 34, verse 27:

﴿Say: "Show me those whom you have joined with Him as partners."﴾ (i.e., inform me of them) ﴿In worship.﴾ ﴿No!﴾ (a rebuke to them for believing in a partner for Him) ﴿Rather, He is Allah, the Almighty﴾ (the Dominant over His affair) ﴿the All-Wise﴾ (in His management of His creation), so there can be no partner for Him in His dominion.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 34, verse 28:

﴿And We have not sent you except comprehensively to mankind﴾ — a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) referring back to "mankind" (al-nās); it has been placed first for emphasis (lil-ihtimām) — ﴿as a bringer of good tidings﴾ — announcing glad tidings to the believers of Paradise — ﴿and a warner﴾ — warning the disbelievers of punishment — ﴿but most of mankind﴾ — i.e., the disbelievers of Makkah — ﴿do not know﴾ that.
And they say, "When is this promise," of punishment, "if you are truthful" about it?
﴿Say: For you is an appointed time, a day from which you cannot delay by an hour, nor can you advance it.﴾ (upon it), and it is the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 34, verse 31:

﴿And those who disbelieved said﴾ from among the people of Makkah, ﴿"We will never believe in this Qur'an, nor in that which came before it"﴾ i.e., that which preceded it, such as the Torah (al-Tawrah) and the Gospel (al-Injil), which affirm the Resurrection, because of their denial of it. ﴿And if you could see﴾ O Muhammad ﴿when the wrongdoers﴾ the disbelievers ﴿will be made to stand before their Lord, sending back the word to one another﴾ ﴿the ones who were oppressed﴾ the followers ﴿will say to those who were arrogant﴾ the leaders ﴿"Were it not for you, we would have been believers"﴾ in the Prophet, ﴿had you not hindered us from faith"﴾ (i.e., you turned us away from faith) ... ﴿we would have been believers﴾ in the Prophet.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 34, verse 32:

﴿Nay, but you were criminals﴾ in yourselves

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 34, verse 33:

﴿And those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant: "Rather, it was the scheming of the night and the day, when you used to command us to disbelieve in Allah and set up rivals to Him."﴾ That is, scheming in them (the night and the day) from you against us. ﴿When you commanded us to disbelieve in Allah and set up rivals (andad)﴾ partners (shuraka'). ﴿And they will conceal﴾ that is, the two groups will conceal ﴿the regret﴾ over abandoning belief in Him ﴿when they see the punishment﴾ that is, each of them will hide it from his companion, fearing reproach. ﴿And We will place shackles on the necks of those who disbelieved﴾ in the Fire. ﴿Will they be recompensed except﴾ with the recompense ﴿for what they used to do﴾ in the worldly life?
﴿And We did not send a warner into any town but that its affluent ones said﴾ (its leaders, the luxury-loving)
﴿And they say, "We have more wealth and children"﴾ than those who believed.

﴿Say: Indeed, my Lord extends provision to whom He wills﴾ widens it ﴿for whom He wills﴾ as a test, ﴿and restricts it﴾ constricts it for whom He wills as a trial, ﴿but most people﴾ i.e., the disbelievers of Mecca ﴿do not know﴾ that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 34, verse 37:

﴿And it is not your wealth nor your children that bring you near to Us in nearness﴾ — qurbā, meaning taqrīban (bringing near). ﴿Except﴾ — that is, but ﴿those who believe and do righteous deeds; for them is the recompense of double (ḍiʿf) for what they have done﴾ — that is, the recompense of the deed: a good deed, for example, is rewarded tenfold or more. ﴿And they will be in the upper chambers (al-ghurufāt)﴾ of Paradise — and in another reading, al-ghurfah, meaning the collective noun — ﴿secure﴾ from death and other things.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on surah 34, verse 38:

﴿And those who strive against Our verses﴾ — those who strive against the Qur'an by trying to nullify it, ﴿seeking to frustrate [Us]﴾ — thinking they can overcome Us, deeming that Our power is incapable of [them], and that they will escape Us.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 34, verse 39:

﴿Say, "Indeed, my Lord extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts it for him"﴾ He widens it ﴿for whom He wills of His servants﴾ as a test, ﴿and restricts it for him﴾ He narrows it ﴿for him﴾ after extending it, or for whom He wills as a trial. ﴿And whatever you spend of anything﴾ in good ﴿He will replace it, and He is the best of providers﴾. It is said: every person provides for his family, meaning from the provision of Allah.

﴿And﴾ ﴿[mention] the Day We will gather them all together﴾, meaning the polytheists (al-mushrikin), ﴿then We will say to the angels: "Are these the ones who used to worship you?"﴾ It is read with the two hamzas (glottal stops) pronounced in full (tahqiq), with the first hamza changed to a yāʾ, and with the first hamza dropped. The words under discussion are أَهَؤُلَاءِ and إِيَّاكُمْ.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 34, verse 41:

﴿They will say: "Glory be to You"﴾, exalting You above having partners (tanzihan laka 'an al-sharik), ﴿"You are our Guardian, not them"﴾, meaning there is no alliance (muwalah) between us and them on our part. ﴿"Rather"﴾ (bal, for transition), ﴿"they used to worship the jinn"﴾, the devils, meaning they obeyed them in their worship of us. ﴿"Most of them believed in them"﴾, meaning they affirmed as true what the devils told them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 34, verse 42:

﴿So today none of you will have power to benefit or harm one another﴾, i.e., some of the worshipped ones for some of the worshippers, ﴿benefit﴾ meaning intercession, ﴿or harm﴾ meaning punishment. ﴿And We will say to those who wronged﴾, meaning those who disbelieved.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 34, verse 43:

﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them﴾, (i.e., the Qur'an) ﴿clear﴾ (i.e., evident), in the tongue of our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿they say: "This is nothing but a man who wants to turn you away from what your fathers used to worship"﴾ of the idols. ﴿And they say: "This is nothing but a fabricated lie"﴾ (i.e., falsehood) ﴿invented against Allah﴾. ﴿And those who disbelieve say of the truth﴾ (i.e., the Qur'an) ﴿when it comes to them: "This is nothing but evident magic"﴾ (i.e., clear).
﴿And We did not give them any books that they study, nor did We send to them, before you, any warner. So from where did they deny you?﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 34, verse 45:

﴿And those before them denied, and they have not attained a tenth of what We had given them﴾ — that is, these (Quraysh) [have not attained] ﴿a tenth of what We had given them﴾ of strength, long life and abundance of wealth. ﴿So they denied My messengers﴾ sent to them, ﴿so how was My rejection﴾ — My disapproval of them, in punishment and destruction. That is, it indeed befell them as it should have.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 34, verse 46:

﴿Say: I admonish you with one thing﴾, which is ﴿that you stand up for Allah﴾, i.e., for His sake, ﴿in pairs﴾, i.e., two by two, ﴿and singly﴾, one by one, ﴿then reflect﴾, so that you may know ﴿what is in your companion﴾, Muhammad, ﴿of madness﴾, insanity. ﴿He is only a warner to you before﴾, i.e., before the arrival of, ﴿a severe punishment﴾ in the Hereafter, ﴿if you disobey Him﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 34, verse 47:

﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿"Whatever reward I have asked of you﴾ for warning and conveying (the message), ﴿it is yours"﴾, i.e., I do not ask you for any reward for it. ﴿"My reward is only with Allah, and He is over all things Witness"﴾, Observer, who knows my truthfulness.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 34, verse 48:

﴿Say: Indeed, my Lord casts down the truth﴾ He casts it (yulqīh, "throws it") to His prophets. ﴿Knower of the unseen﴾ (ʿallām al-ghuyūb), that which is hidden from His creation in the heavens and the earth.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 34, verse 49:

﴿Say: The truth has come,﴾ meaning Islam, ﴿and falsehood can neither originate nor restore,﴾ meaning disbelief, ﴿and it can neither originate nor restore,﴾ that is, no trace of it remains.

﴿Say, "If I go astray﴾ from the truth ﴿then I only go astray to my own detriment﴾, meaning the sin of my going astray falls upon me. ﴿And if I am guided, it is by what my Lord reveals to me﴾ of the Qur'an and the wisdom (ḥikmah, sound understanding and practice). ﴿Indeed, He is All-Hearing﴾ of the supplication."

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 34, verse 51:

﴿And if you could see﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿when they are seized with terror﴾ at the Resurrection, you would see a tremendous matter. ﴿Then there is no escape﴾ for them from Us, meaning they will not escape Us. ﴿And they will be seized from a near place﴾, meaning the graves.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 34, verse 52:**

﴿And they will say, "We believe in Him"﴾ — in Muhammad or the Qur'an. ﴿But how can they reach [the belief] from a distant place?﴾ — al-tanawush is read with a waw, and with a hamza in its place; i.e., the taking hold of (tanawul) faith. ﴿From a place far away﴾ — far from the place of faith, since they are in the Hereafter, whereas the place of faith is this world (al-dunya).

﴿And they had already disbelieved in it before﴾ in the world, ﴿and they would hurl [ya-qdhifuna] (يَرْمُونَ, "cast/throw") ﴿at the unseen from a far place﴾, i.e., at that which its knowledge was far hidden from them, a distant concealment, when they said about the Prophet: "A sorcerer, a poet, a soothsayer," and about the Qur'an: "Sorcery, poetry, soothsaying."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 34, verse 54:

﴿And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire﴾ of faith, i.e., its acceptance, ﴿just as was done to their likes﴾ their counterparts in disbelief ﴿before﴾ i.e., before them. ﴿Indeed, they were in disquieting doubt﴾ causing suspicion (mawqi' fi al-rayba) for them, regarding what they now believe in, and they did not heed its proofs in the world.
